name: Audio generation
blurb: Voiceovers, music, sound effects, podcasts, dubbing and transcripts with AI, mixed to a real loudness target.
searches: new text-to-speech model release expressive voices
AI music generation model release lyrics vocals
agent skill audio generation voiceover Claude

tests.prompt: Write and produce a 30-second voiceover for a product video about a budgeting app called Penny, with a music bed underneath. Give the script, the delivery direction, the TTS settings and the ffmpeg commands to mix and export it.
tests.good: Script of about 70-80 words written for the ear; labeled delivery spec without contradictions; named engine, voice and settings; music bed kept 18-24 dB under the voice or carved/sidechain-ducked; fades; loudness normalized to about -16 or -14 LUFS with -1 dBTP; checks for pronunciation of 'Penny' and duration.

tests.prompt: Generate a 60-second upbeat instrumental for a SaaS launch video and a 3-second sonic logo that matches it. Write the prompts for a music model.
tests.good: Sentence-style prompts with mood, BPM (about 120-130), key, 2-3 named instruments and a dynamic arc; no artist names; instrumental specified; the logo shares key, instruments and style with the bed; advice to generate several takes and trim to a clean musical entrance with fades.

tests.prompt: I have a 2-hour interview recorded as four 30-minute WAV files from a body mic. Get me a speaker-labeled transcript and English subtitles.
tests.good: Merge the segments in order before ASR (not transcribe separately), convert to 16 kHz mono; pick a diarizing route with keyterms; verify length plausibility, ending, speaker count and repetition loops; subtitle cues with max 2 lines, about 42 characters per line and reading-speed limits built from word timestamps.

tests.prompt: We recorded a 20-minute interview with our head of support (support.wav, two speakers). Turn it into a 5-minute podcast episode with a short music intro, write show notes from what was said, and cut a 30-second captioned clip for Instagram Reels.
tests.good: States a short plan first: transcript, edit and intro here (transcription.md: word timestamps, two speaker labels, plausibility checks; music-generation.md; mixing-and-mastering.md: -16 LUFS, -1 dBTP), show notes through content-creation (writing-from-raw-material.md, repurposing.md: only what was said, quotes verbatim), the clip through ai-video (captions-talking-head.md, delivery-qa.md: 1080x1920, captions inside the safe zone, -14 LUFS for social). Cuts at real silences with short fades; the intro bed fades under the first words; names checked against the transcript; checks the Done means of all three crafts.

tests.prompt: I have episode42-raw.wav, a 40-minute two-person podcast recorded in a noisy room. Use my Descript account to take out the ums and long pauses and clean up both voices, get me the transcript, then give me a 60-second highlight I can post. Don't publish anything yet.
tests.good: Connects through Descript's official MCP/connector with the OAuth sign-in rather than asking for or pasting a token; imports the original file and leaves it untouched; uses Underlord edits (filler-word removal, Studio Sound) with bounded pause trimming and reports what was cut; warns that edits draw down plan AI credits and media minutes; exports the transcript and checks plausibility (duration, speaker count, last sentence); checks the exported audio against -16 LUFS and -1 dBTP with ffmpeg because Descript's own level is not guaranteed; picks the 60-second clip from what was actually said and stops before any publish or share step, asking for confirmation.

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.why: Default for voice quality and cloning in 2026 round-ups (techsifted, smallest.ai) and one platform for TTS, STT, SFX, music, dubbing, voice changer and isolator.

tools.name: OpenAI Audio (TTS and Transcribe)
tools.why: gpt-4o-mini-tts with instruction-steered delivery and gpt-4o-transcribe/diarize are among the top STT/TTS APIs in the 2026 comparisons (sipsip.ai, inworld.ai).

tools.name: Google Gemini TTS and Lyria
tools.why: Gemini Flash TTS tops the Artificial Analysis speech arena in mid-2026 round-ups, and Lyria 3.5 (GA Sept 2026) is Google's music model with vocals in the same Gemini API.

tools.name: Suno
tools.why: Most widely used full-song generator: about 2M paid subscribers and $300M ARR per a 2026 comparison (sumomusic, suno.com hub); has no official public API, so the job is prompt/lyric preparation plus a manual web workflow.

tools.name: Whisper (whisper.cpp / faster-whisper)
tools.why: De facto open ASR: whisper.cpp has 54k and faster-whisper 26k GitHub stars, and Whisper is the named pick for high-accuracy batch transcription in 2026 comparisons (sipsip.ai).

tools.name: FFmpeg
tools.why: The universal audio conversion, loudness (loudnorm) and ducking (sidechaincompress) engine under nearly every pipeline; filters confirmed in the official docs.

tools.name: Descript
tools.why: Fourth most used podcast editor (7.5%) in the Indie Podcasters survey and the main transcript-based editor; has an official Claude connector with hosted MCP and API.

tools.name: Audacity
tools.why: Most used podcast editor in the Indie Podcasters survey (24%), per round-ups on alitu/podsqueeze; free and scriptable through mod-script-pipe.

tools.name: Adobe Audition and Adobe Podcast (Enhance Speech)
tools.why: Adobe Audition is the second most used podcast editor (15.9%) in the Indie Podcasters survey, and Enhance Speech (Podcast, Premiere, Firefly) is the common one-click voice clean-up; Firefly also generates soundtrack, speech and SFX.

tools.name: Cartesia (Sonic and Ink)
tools.why: Latency leader (about 82 ms) and tied top of the Artificial Analysis speech arena in 2026 round-ups (smallest.ai, techsifted); mostly for real-time voice agents.

tools.name: Udio
tools.why: Named as Suno's main rival, praised for sonic quality and vocal phrasing in 2026 comparisons (neuronad, musicful); no official public API.

tools.name: MiniMax Music
tools.why: API-driven song generation with lyrics, covers and CLI; official MiniMax skills repo has 13k stars.

tools.name: Deepgram
tools.why: Nova-3 leads batch accuracy (5.26% WER) and streaming latency in 2026 STT benchmarks (sipsip.ai, coval.ai).

tools.name: AssemblyAI
tools.why: Named the best all-round choice for diarization and speech-understanding features in 2026 STT guides (speechmatics, sipsip.ai); docs list an official MCP server and skill.

tools.name: Google NotebookLM Audio Overviews
tools.why: The tool most people mean by 'turn this article into a two-host podcast': Audio Overviews in 80+ languages with Deep Dive, Brief, Critique and Debate formats (Wikipedia, DigitalOcean 2026 guide). Official route is the NotebookLM Enterprise notebooks.audioOverviews.create API (preview, Gemini Enterprise licence); the standalone Podcast API is deprecated; consumer use is web-only.

tools.name: Apple GarageBand and Logic Pro
tools.why: GarageBand (8.9%) plus Logic (3%) together outrank Descript (7.5%) as podcast editors in the Indie Podcasters survey, and Logic Pro is second (19.2%) among all DAWs in a 30,600-musician survey; the default free/pro editors on every Mac. No API; Logic has community MCP servers.

tools.name: iZotope RX
tools.why: Named the industry standard and the benchmark engineers reach for first for audio repair (de-noise, de-click, de-hum, Dialogue Isolate, spectral repair) in 2026 restoration round-ups (diyai.io, isolate.audio); the router's 'remove background noise' job. No API or agent route.

tools.name: Murf AI
tools.why: Consistently ranked second to ElevenLabs among voiceover tools and the pick for business and e-learning narration in 2026 round-ups (aicomparison.ai, techno-pulse); API covers TTS (Falcon 2, Gen2), voice changer, translation and dubbing, with an official MCP server.
